articles.headline: NFL Week 2 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines
articles.description: Will Ashton Jeanty pile up the scrimmage yards? Could the Bengals upset the Texans? And can George Pickens find the end zone?
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season is off to an exciting start, as the Bills defeated the Lions 41-31 in the first game at Highmark Stadium. But what will happen in the remaining 15 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projected out stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody gives three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen suggests three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Could the Bengals upset the Texans? Will we see big receiving days for the Dolphins' Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas? Can Eagles running back Saquon Barkley find the end zone? And is it finally time for the Jets to snag an interception? Let's make 15 big predictions for all of Sunday and Monday's action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

TD scorers | Other predictions

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Jacksonville Jaguars +2.5 at Denver Broncos (+124)

Denver's offense hasn't shown enough to justify laying points. The Broncos produced only 176 yards and 3.7 yards per play in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, with quarterback Bo Nix turning it over twice. Jacksonville is bringing a pass rush that generated five sacks against Cleveland, while QB Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes. Defense makes the Broncos the favorite, but the Jaguars have the more trustworthy offense to win outright.

Cincinnati Bengals +2.5 at Houston Texans (+120)

The Bengals' biggest weakness looked better against the Bucs, as quarterback Joe Burrow was sacked only once. If that holds, he gets a Houston defense that just allowed 10.4 yards per pass to Buffalo in Week 1. Houston can obviously pressure Burrow, but if Cincinnati's offensive line continues to improve, it should have enough through the air with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

Walder predicts three stat lines

Rhamondre Stevenson, RB, New England Patriots: 16 carries, 63 rushing yards; 5 receptions, 42 receiving yards, 1 receiving touchdown

Since 2023, running backs catch passes on 8% of dropbacks against man coverage but 15% against zone coverage. Why does that matter here? Because in Week 1 against the Falcons, the Steelers ran zone coverage 89% of the time under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham. So I expect Stevenson to have a big day in the receiving game.

And while I don't expect the Patriots will be as run-heavy as they were in Week 1 -- which certainly didn't work out for them! -- New England should be ahead by enough early to run the ball late in the game. All in all, it should be a healthy workload for Stevenson.

Riq Woolen, CB, Philadelphia Eagles: 34 coverage snaps, 1 reception allowed for 7 yards on four targets, 1 interception

articles.headline: European soccer live updates: Tottenham, Aston Villa both chasing first win
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are looking for their first Premier League win of the season, as another weekend of European soccer begins.
articles.body:
It's another weekend of European soccer and the final one before the international break!

In the Premier League, Saturday's action begins with Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa facing off as both teams chase their first win of the season. Later, Brighton & Hove Albion host leaders and defending champions Arsenal in a clash between two teams near the top of the table. Finally, Nottingham Forest host a Coventry City side still searching for their first win and goal of the season.

Elsewhere, AS Roma host Inter Milan in a huge clash between Serie A's current top two. In the Bundesliga, Stuttgart take on Borussia Dortmund, while in LaLiga, Sevilla host league leaders Barcelona.

Enjoy all the updates from Saturday's matches.

articles.headline: Who is Commanders' special teams ace Tyler Owens?
articles.description: J.J. Watt called Owens' play against the Eagles 'legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen.'
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The play, viewed more than 18 million times on one social media platform, went like this: Washington Commanders special-teamer Tyler Owens, ready to cover a punt, stepped outside then cut back inside and ripped through a double-team at the line of scrimmage. He flung one blocker to the side then stiff-armed the other as he raced downfield. When the other blocker caught back up to Owens, he shoved him to the ground then did the same to the second one.

Owens looked like a man chasing someone stealing his car.

And then Owens reached the returner, who decided to leap. Bad decision. Owens corralled him and body-slammed him to the ground. Owens then got up and casually walked to the sideline, as if he had just clocked out of work for the day.

"It was just a good rep," he said.

Others begged to differ. Former Pro Bowl defensive end J.J. Watt called it "legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen." It has been viewed more than 11.6 million times on the NFL's X feed and another 6.9 million times on the NFLmemes feed. More than 40,000 people liked it on the NFL's Instagram page.

"I was just out there playing football," Owens said. "It never really stood out to me until after."

And though it introduced Owens to the sporting world, his teammates needed no introductions. They already knew what he could do -- and has done. They might have been impressed by the play, but they were not surprised.

There's a reason Owens made the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024; he made two plays that summer to stand out. Those plays also prompted coach Dan Quinn to make an unusual announcement in a team meeting about Owens. His special teams coach at Texas Tech, Kenny Perry, could point to plays in college that prompted him to tell Owens he would make a long living in the NFL.

"That's what he's been doing," said Washington safety Jeremy Reaves, a special teams Pro Bowler after the 2022 season. "He's done that over and over and over again. That's who he is."

Commanders punter Tress Way, who has been in the league since 2014, said he gets the same question from coordinators or assistant coaches on other teams.

"Just about every team we play, they're like, 'What do you guys feed 18?'" Way said. "I tell them punt returners."

Three days after the play, after he had become a teaching tool for special teams coaches at every level and after seeing the reaction and appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show," Owens knows it was more than "just a good rep."

And though other plays stand out in his mind, this one vs. the Eagles vaulted to the top.

"I would say this is my favorite," Owens said. "Just because of the physicality. ... It's just rewarding. You put in all this work, finally get to see something come out of it."

What he saw was a viral reaction.

"Just all the GOATS retweeting it and stuff like that. It's pretty dope," Owens said. "I like it."

articles.headline: How the 49ers are readjusting after weeklong Australia trip
articles.description: On their 16-hour flight home from Australia, the 49ers chose sleep over celebration. That kick-started a long week of getting back into routine.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- After a convincing 27-7 win over a division rival, the San Francisco 49ers boarded their buses and headed to the Melbourne airport with visions of a victory party dancing in their heads.

The Niners knew they couldn't take off before the Los Angeles Rams' departed, but they still had every intention of making the most of the 16-hour flight home. But by the time they boarded the plane, all of those plans stayed on the ground, as adrenaline gave way to the fatigue from their weeklong trip down under.

"We're all like, dude, we're going to fall asleep and then we're going to wake up and we're going to celebrate," fullback Kyle Juszczyk said. "We're going to have our team party that we didn't get to have. And then I woke up like an hour before we got there, and everyone was still sleeping. I don't think anybody celebrated."

While they had every reason to celebrate in the moment, the fact that they didn't should only help them overcome the final obstacle of the Australia trip: reacclimating to Pacific time and a normal workweek.

Asked this week whether it was more difficult to adjust to Australian time or readjusting to Pacific time, there were players on both sides of the fence. But they all agreed there was at least a little bit of an adjustment period.

"Speaking for myself, I felt like crap all weekend," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "We had two days off and I did not feel right. Took a couple of days. I think I was good by Monday. Talking to some of the guys, some guys felt fine right away. Some went through the same stuff, but I think we're definitely all good by now."

Much like they did for the flight to Melbourne, the Niners had recovery plans for their players that began as soon as they stepped back on the Qantas A380 plane. Dustin Perry, the team's vice president of player health and performance, and his staff provided players with instructions on how much water to drink on the plane, how long to stay up before falling asleep and when to wake up.

Right tackle Colton McKivitz said the objective was to stay up for a couple of hours (an easy enough task with so much adrenaline still pumping from the game), go to sleep in their lie-flat seats, and then wake up for the final few hours of the flight.

McKivitz estimated he slept for about seven hours. Running back Christian McCaffrey said he was out for about 13 hours, which was about the same as rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton. Defensive end Nick Bosa was in the same range.

"I actually felt it worse on the way back," Bosa said. "Going out, you just kind of power through a few hours and then go to bed early and then just stay on a little earlier wake-up is what I did. And then when I came back, it's been kind of hard to get to bed, but [Tuesday] night I got to bed nice and early."

articles.headline: First impressions of Raiders' defense under Rob Leonard
articles.description: After a Week 1 win, players praised how the new DC called the defense against Miami.
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Throughout the offseason, first-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard didn't want to dive too much into how the Las Vegas Raiders' defense would look under his guidance.

It was obvious that the Raiders wanted to be versatile, given the handful of players who can line up at different spots on the field, and they wanted to be aggressive when pursuing the quarterback. But Leonard steered away from revealing his full plans, especially during preseason games, by keeping things basic until the Raiders were in matchups that counted.

In the Raiders' Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins, Leonard didn't hold back in his playcalling, and the results were good. Las Vegas put together a promising defensive performance by containing Miami's run game and making quarterback Malik Willis' life uncomfortable in the pocket. More importantly, the Raiders' 27-13 victory showed that they have a solid supporting cast around All-Pro defensive end Maxx Crosby.

"I think he called a great game, and we just got to keep getting better because there's definitely some things we can improve on," Crosby said.

The numbers were impressive. Everything that was an issue for the unit last season became a strength. The Dolphins were held to 74 rushing yards despite having the upper hand in this category going into the season opener because of running back De'Von Achane. And even he had only 36 yards on 11 carries.

The Raiders limited Miami to converting 3 of 10 attempts on third down. On top of that, the Dolphins scored just one touchdown on three red zone trips. The Raiders also forced two turnovers.

The biggest takeaway, however, was being able to pressure Willis. In Week 1, the Raiders tied for the most sacks (five) in the league, had the fifth-most pressures (15) and had the sixth-best pressure rate at 44.4%.

"[Leonard] emphasizes allowing us to have a lot of confidence with the calls and be able to execute at a high level," defensive lineman Thomas Booker IV told ESPN. "Violence is speed. I think that's the big calling card of the defense."

Eight players recorded a pressure, including Crosby and Kwity Paye -- who combined for 3.5 sacks, 11 pressures and 10 quarterback hits. One play in the fourth quarter showcased a good playcall from Leonard and how strong Las Vegas' defense can be with Paye and Crosby lining up on opposite sides.

With the Dolphins facing a third-and-10 at the 11-minute mark of the quarter, Las Vegas rushed five defenders. When Achane attempted to block linebacker Quay Walker, Paye looped inside while Crosby forcefully pushed off offensive tackle Austin Jackson. Paye and Crosby then combined to take down Willis for a sack.

Paye's performance alone was a breath of fresh air. The Raiders needed a secondary pass rusher. They spent last season relying heavily on Crosby to be the anchor in stopping the pass and run game.

articles.headline: Dolphins not discouraged by Chris Johnson's rough stat sheet
articles.description: Coach Jeff Hafley found positives for first-round cornerback Chris Johnson despite a hard day at the office.
articles.body:
NAPA, Calif. -- According to The Associated Press, Miami Dolphins rookies played more snaps in Week 1 than any team since at least 2006; unsurprising for the league's youngest team.

While linebacker Jacob Rodriguez and wide receiver Caleb Douglas were among Miami's standout performers in Sunday's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, cornerback Chris Johnson's day wasn't as smooth -- at least on paper.

The first-round pick was targeted 11 times, according to NextGen Stats, allowing six catches for 62 yards. He was also the nearest defender on two of Kirk Cousins' touchdown passes.

But teammates and coaches say Johnson's performance was more than what the stat sheet suggested, and they know the rookie's confidence won't waver going into this week's matchup with the San Francisco 49ers (4:25 p.m. ET on Fox).

"I think Chris, when you watch the tape and you look at the scheme and you don't just point fingers at a guy who you think was at fault -- I think there's certainly some plays that Chris wants back," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "I think Chris showed a lot of flashes and played a solid game. He was good against a run at his nickel position. ... He's hard on himself, too, because he's the one that it's showing up on. Chris did a lot of good things [Sunday] and Chris should be confident that he can do a lot of good things in this league."

Johnson was in coverage on Cousins' touchdown passes to Jack Bech and Ashton Jeanty, but Hafley said neither score was actually his fault based on scheme responsibilities.

Miami was in Cover 1 on Bech's touchdown catch, which features a deep safety and sometimes a "robber," where either the other safety or a linebacker covers shorter routes over the middle of the field. Safety Zayne Anderson and linebacker Jordyn Brooks both covered Raiders tight end Michael Mayer, and Bech scored on a slant route directly to the area of the field Anderson vacated.

The Dolphins were also in Cover 1 on Jeanty's touchdown and the Raiders took advantage of a similar mistake -- this time, Brooks and rookie safety Michael Taaffe both covered Mayer, and Cousins found Jeanty in the space that Taaffe vacated.

"Really just have to clean up some of my techniques," Johnson said after the game. "I feel like I was responsible for a few touchdowns but at the end of the day, I've got to be cleaner in my coverage. The team is relying on me to do that."

Taaffe told reporters that he was responsible for one of the touchdowns attributed to Johnson but didn't clarify which one. Hafley said the players who missed their assignments immediately owned up to it on the sideline after each play.

Johnson did finish with 11 tackles in his NFL regular-season debut, as well as two pass breakups and an impressive tackle for a loss where he wrapped Jeanty up behind the line of scrimmage on the Raiders' first offensive drive.

articles.headline: Eagles' new perspective for '26: Don't 'let anyone steal our joy'
articles.description: It's no coincidence the mood inside Philly's locker room was at its most sullen in 2023 and '25, two seasons following Super Bowl runs.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia Eagles beat the Washington Commanders 24-22 in the season opener and were consciously making an effort in the game's aftermath to let that be enough.

"Last year, I know everyone [would] try to make something of, we won by two points. We're not getting on that this year. And that's a beautiful thing," running back Saquon Barkley said. "We come out with a win, we're going to be happy, we're going to celebrate and we're going to flush it and move on and get ready for next week."

That was the core of coach Nick Sirianni's postgame message to the team, players said: that, as receiver/returner Britain Covey put it, "We're not going to let anyone steal our joy from the wins."

Philadelphia has felt like Whoville at times in recent years, with inflated expectations and over analysis swiping the gift of victory with a Grinch-like harshness.

Such an environment -- where there's such angst over a four-year stretch in which the team has gone 51-18, reached two Super Bowl and won one -- is only possible when outsized standards are enforced by members of the organization and its city alike. And it's no coincidence that the mood inside the locker room and out was at its most sullen in 2023 and '25, two seasons following Super Bowl runs when good was in the shadows of great.

Barkley said he tried his best not to compare his more-than-respectable 2025 campaign (1,140 rushing yards, 7 TDs) to '24, when he became just the ninth back ever to eclipse 2,000 yards in the regular season, but "human nature" sometimes got the better of him.

He credits the team psychiatrist, Dr. Jody Foster, for helping to shift his mindset. Barkley told ESPN that the pivotal conversation with Foster occurred on the bus ride from the hotel to Gillette Stadium in front of the Eagles' preseason game against the New England Patriots on Aug. 22. She encouraged him to recognize the small wins during the course of a game or a season and to focus on three or four short-term goals within his control instead of overly concerning himself with the big picture.

"She's really just trying to get me focused on just getting back to the process and falling in love with the process. It's so easy in this business and who I am as a person to get motivated or pushed by results," he said, "but in reality, that's not what it's about."

Winning, Sirianni reminded the gathered media Wednesday, is hard, and he used a "Seinfeld" reference to illustrate his point.

He noted the Paul O'Neill episode, in which Kramer promises a child in the hospital that the Yankees slugger will hit two home runs for him in one game. "It's hard to hit home runs, and where did you get two from?" O'Neill asks Kramer, who snuck into the clubhouse.

In other words, winning is hard enough; there's no need to throw qualifiers on top of it when seeking satisfaction.

articles.headline: Liverpool's Andoni Iraola admits Bournemouth will be aware of his tactics ahead of 'tricky' return
articles.description: Andoni Iraola is looking forward to returning to Bournemouth with Liverpool -- even if the opponents may understand his methods better than his own players.
articles.headlineJa: リヴァプールのアンドニ・イラオラ監督、古巣ボーンマスへの「一筋縄ではいかない」復帰戦を前に相手が自身の戦術を把握していると認める
articles.descriptionJa: アンドニ・イラオラは、対戦相手の方が自分のチームの選手よりも自身の戦術をよく理解しているかもしれないとしても、リヴァプールを率いてボーンマスに帰還することを楽しみにしている。
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola is looking forward to returning to Bournemouth with Liverpool -- even if the opponents may understand his methods better than his own players.

The Spaniard is six games into his reign as Liverpool manager after leaving the Cherries, whom he guided into Europe for the first time at the end of last season.

His new side are unbeaten so far, although performances have been mixed.

That record will be put to the test as Liverpool travel to the Vitality Stadium in the Premier League on Sunday, and Iraola admits it will be a strange feeling.

He said: "On the personal side I am really looking forward to meeting them, to hug them. They are players that I love, staff that I worked with and appreciate so much.

"I was buzzing for them when they played their first European game. I wish them all the best but there is another part -- and that is the most important one -- that we need to go there and win and be as ruthless as possible, and leave all the talk for after the game.

"It is going to be a tricky one. They know, obviously, very well what we are trying to do.

"But I also know their strengths and their weaknesses. So you never know who has the most advantage in that sense, but it is going to be different."

One advantage Iraola accepts his side do have, however, is in the preparation.

Liverpool have had two extra days' rest following Tuesday's Carabao Cup win over Tottenham, while Bournemouth were in action on Thursday as they made their Europa League bow against Real Sociedad.

"I think we have an advantage," he said. "Most of the times it has been the opposite. We have been the team that played the last, but this time we played two days before they played.

"I think there should be an advantage there but also I know where we are going, and I know what they have there, not only the stadium but overall.

"When you see the number of games they have lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth."

Liverpool may still be finding their feet under Iraola, but one player to have settled quickly is defender Ronald Araújo.

The Uruguay international has moved to Anfield on a season-long loan from Barcelona, where he had been captain, and immediately impressed Iraola with his fitness level and versatility.

articles.description: Noni Madueke could leave for one of Arsenal's Premier League rivals in January in a search for more playing time. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：アーセナルのマドゥエケにプレミアリーグのライバルクラブが関心
articles.descriptionJa: ノニ・マドゥエケは、より多くの出場時間を求めて1月にアーセナルのプレミアリーグにおけるライバルクラブへ移籍する可能性がある。移籍情報を扱う『Transfer Talk』が最新情報をお伝えする。
articles.body:
Noni Madueke could leave for one of Arsenal's Premier League rivals in January, while AZ Alkmaar midfielder Kees Smit is on Liverpool's radar. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Several unnamed Premier League sides are monitoring the future of Noni Madueke as a January exit from Arsenal could be on the cards, according to Football Insider. The England international could leave the Emirates Stadium if the Gunners are open to it, as he is struggling for minutes in the early weeks of the season. Madueke, 24, only moved to Arsenal last summer from Chelsea, since when he has scored nine goals and registered four assists in 48 appearances. However, with youngster Max Dowman adding to the competition in his position on the right flank, another move could be on the cards.

- Liverpool are among a whole host of teams tracking AZ Alkmaar midfielder Kees Smit, TEAMtalk reports. The 20-year-old has been a regular for the Dutch side over the past two seasons, with this campaign offering him a chance to impress in the Eredivisie and the Europa League once again. Liverpool are long-term admirers of Smit, who made his senior debut for Netherlands in March but did not make the cut for their 2026 FIFA World Cup squad.

- Arsenal are following the progress of Sturm Graz youngster Luca Weinhandl, along with fellow Premier League clubs Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion, according to TEAMtalk. The 17-year-old made his breakthrough last season with 10 appearances in the Austrian Bundesliga. This season he has already seen him feature five times, along with a start in the Europa League. A £20 million package could reportedly be enough to land Weinhandl, as teams position themselves for the January transfer window.

- New York City FC is closing in on the signing of defender Matt Miazga as a free agent, days after FC Cincinnati waived his contract, The Athletic reports. The 31-year-old is closing in on the switch with NYCFC aiming for a place in this season's playoffs. Miazga, who has won 28 caps for the USMNT, has plenty of experience in MLS, and was named the MLS Defender of the Year in 2023. After 108 appearances with Cincinnati, the former Chelsea man will now be looking to make an impact with NYCFC.

- Juventus are preparing talks with Nicolás González over a contract extension during the upcoming international break. Nicolo Schira states that the winger could sign for an extra year or two, with his current deal running until 2029. González spent last season on loan at Atlético Madrid, and while an approach was made for the 28-year-old by the Rojiblancos, as well as Inter Milan and a Saudi Pro League team, he decided to stay at the club. The forward has two goals and one assist to his name in four appearances since returning to Turin, as he looks to consolidate that form with a new contract.

articles.headline: Inter Milan, Italy great Sandro Mazzola dies at 83: 'An eternal symbol'
articles.description: Inter Milan have paid tribute to one-club man and Italy great Sandro Mazzola after his death at the age of 83.
articles.headlineJa: インテルとイタリアの偉人サンドロ・マッツォーラ氏が83歳で死去：「永遠の象徴」
articles.descriptionJa: インテル・ミラノは、生涯一クラブを貫きイタリアの偉大な存在であったサンドロ・マッツォーラ氏が83歳で死去したことを受け、追悼の意を表した。
articles.body:
Inter Milan have paid tribute to one-club man and Italy great Sandro Mazzola after his death at the age of 83.

The striker won four Serie A titles and two European Cups with Inter across his near 20 years with the San Siro side, while Mazzola also won the European Championship with Italy in 1968 and was a World Cup runner-up two years later in 1970.

Inter said on X: "There are those who enter history. And then there are those who become the very history of Inter itself.

"From a young Nerazzurri boy to an eternal symbol, Sandro Mazzola has spanned generations, winning, thrilling, and passing down the love for these colours.

"He shone on the field, and he shines even now, the star with the moustache. Who, as he often said, had just one, final wish: To be remembered as a good man, who always gives his all, even when it seems impossible."

Mazzola made 567 appearances for Inter, scoring 161 goals, between 1960 and 1977 and founded the Italian Footballers' Association in 1968. He scored 22 goals for Italy over 70 caps.

He later worked as a sporting director at Inter and Torino and also as a commentator, notably covering Italy's World Cup final victories in both 1982 and 2006.
